current_activity: lands from rubber boats on Levant (2nd and 3rd Regiments) and Port-Cros (1st Regiment); Levant clear by 2030
notes: Event date: 15 August 1944, from about 0030 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 6). Event definition: Carried from Corsica in Task Force 86, the force lands just after midnight on the Hyères islands, the 1st Regiment on Port-Cros and the 2nd and 3rd Regiments on the east shore of Levant; tactical surprise is complete and fighting on Levant is over by 2030 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 6; Wikipedia). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 6, p. 98: "while the 2d and 3d Regiments made their assault along the eastern shore of Levant"; Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 6, p. 98: "all fighting was over on Levant by 2030 that evening"; Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Force: "landed on the islands of Port Cros and Île du Levant during Operation Dragoon". Location: Île du Levant, Var (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith and Wikipedia name Levant and Port-Cros. Commander: Colonel Edwin A. Walker (Clarke and Smith, chs. 3 and 5; Wikipedia). Context: Wikipedia dates the landing 14 August; the boats left the ships at 2300 on the 14th and reached the shore after midnight (Clarke and Smith), so 15 August is used.

current_activity: 1st Regiment takes Port-Cros after the battleship Ramillies shells the fort
notes: Event date: 17 August 1944, late morning (Clarke and Smith, ch. 6). Event definition: On Port-Cros the garrison holds out in the old forts until, late on the morning of 17 August, twelve 15-inch rounds from HMS Ramillies end the resistance (Clarke and Smith, ch. 6). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 6, p. 99: "The capture of Port Cros cost the 1st Special Service Force 5 men killed and 10 wounded". Location: Port-Cros, Var (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith name Port-Cros. Commander: Colonel Edwin A. Walker (Clarke and Smith, chs. 3 and 5; Wikipedia).

current_activity: in the centre of the 1st Airborne Task Force, takes Villeneuve-Loubet after hard fighting
notes: Event date: 26 August 1944 (Wikipedia). Event definition: With the 1st Airborne Task Force, in the centre of its advance east along the coast (Wikipedia, 517th page), the force captures Villeneuve-Loubet on 26 August, one of the villages it had most difficulty taking (Wikipedia). Event support: one source family (Wikipedia). Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Force: "the Force was attached to 1st Airborne Task Force"; "it is one of the villages that the 1st SSF had the hardest time capturing in southern France, on 26 August 1944"; Wikipedia, 517th Parachute Regimental Combat Team: "the Special Service Force the center". Location: Villeneuve-Loubet, Alpes-Maritimes (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Villeneuve-Loubet. Commander: Colonel Edwin A. Walker (Clarke and Smith, chs. 3 and 5; Wikipedia). Context: Relationship: the Seventh Army operational control of the assault is closed the day before (inferred value). Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).

current_activity: with the 1st Airborne Task Force, holds the southern third of the Franco-Italian Alpine front
notes: Event date: mid-October 1944 (approximate date: Clarke and Smith, ch. 20). Event definition: In mid-October the 1st Airborne Task Force, including the Canadian-American 1st Special Service Force, holds the southern third of the Alpine front (Clarke and Smith, ch. 20). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 20, p. 357: "The American 1st Airborne Task Force, including the Canadian-American 1st Special Service Force, held the southern third of the front". Location: Menton, Alpes-Maritimes (new place), a representative point with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: representative point (inferred value): Menton, at the coastal end of the frontier; the date 15 October stands for mid-October (inferred value). Location support: Clarke and Smith give only the southern third of the front. Commander: Colonel Edwin A. Walker (Clarke and Smith, chs. 3 and 5; Wikipedia). Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).

current_activity: disbanded in a field near Villeneuve-Loubet
notes: Event date: 5 December 1944 (Wikipedia); formally 6 January 1945 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 30, n. 32). Event definition: The force is disbanded on 5 December 1944 in a field near Villeneuve-Loubet (Wikipedia); Clarke and Smith say it was relieved shortly after the task force headquarters was dissolved (about 25 November) and formally disbanded on 6 January 1945, the Canadians returning to their national command and the Americans going to the 474th Infantry. Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 30, p. 581: "The Special Service Force units were formally disbanded on 6 January 1945"; Wikipedia, 1st Special Service Force: "The 1st SSF was disbanded 5 December 1944 in a field near Villeneuve-Loubet". Location: Villeneuve-Loubet, Alpes-Maritimes (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Villeneuve-Loubet. Location caveat: the sources differ on the date: the disbandment parade of 5 December (Wikipedia) is used; the formal date is 6 January 1945 (Clarke and Smith). Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded; this row asserts the end of that attachment on 23 November 1944, with the dissolution of the task force, before the row's own date (Brigades Batch 2).
